body:
Note: not sure whether this is bug or not, but there's a breaking change on Docker setup in 1.30.x which is not documented.

## Expected Behavior
The enabled services should follow the value specified in the `SERVICES` environment variable.

## Actual Behavior
All services (frontend, history, matching, worker) is started when starting the Temporal docker on 1.30.x even though `SERVICES` environment variable is set.

## Steps to Reproduce the Problem

  1. Start the v1.30.x docker with `SERVICES` specified (e.g. "frontend")
  2. History, matching, and worker also initialized in the Docker.

## Specifications

  - Version: 1.30.x
  - Platform: All platform.

## Additional context
Before version 1.30.x, there was a script named `start-temporal.sh` ([ref](https://github.com/temporalio/docker-builds/blob/d0ab85e186018d8bbf57e3dc52f1e24944933502/docker/start-temporal.sh)) which parse the `SERVICES` environment variable into `--services=<service_name>` when starting the docker.

On 1.30.x, the script was removed and replaced with `TEMPORAL_SERVICES` ([ref](https://github.com/temporalio/temporal/blob/5f54744bf78e2c114ff92d604fe12ba13aef19fc/cmd/server/main.go#L141)) env variable and the entrypoint.sh is not parsing `SERVICES` env variable when starting the server ([ref](https://github.com/temporalio/temporal/blob/5f54744bf78e2c114ff92d604fe12ba13aef19fc/docker/scripts/sh/entrypoint.sh#L16)). This is not backward compatible, and made Temporal to start all services and consumes more memory than necessary.

This is not backward compatible, and made Temporal to start all services and consumes more memory than necessary.

This change was intentional but we failed to mention it directly in the 1.30.1 release notes. The Helm Charts were updated to use the new variable and I pushed an update to `temporalio/samples-server` that includes the correct variable usage.
This was a missing bit I learned in this thread. Thank you for writing it here!

title: Environment variable `SERVICES` not being read in v1.30.x docker
